Efforts. This program is being proposed to the Department of Energy (DOE) under the Grid 
Resilience Innovative Partnerships (GRIP) Program Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) 
Number: DE-FOA-0003195. Through this proposed program, APS will be able to take proven 
measures to fortify Arizona’s electric grid operations against the threat of wildfires in Arizona. 
In order to significantly enhance the health, safety and well-being of Arizonans, this funding 
would allow APS to complete important initiatives in an expedited timeframe.  
 
Through the support of DOE funding, APS will be able to deploy these important fire mitigation 
tactics in areas of the state that are most in need, enhancing reliability for 289,000 customers. 
Those in rural communities who may have longer or more frequent outages due to Arizona’s fire 
landscape will see fewer disruptions to their daily life. It is clear to Navajo County that this 
project will provide economic and quality-of-life enhancing benefits to the people and 
communities of Arizona.  
 
Navajo County is hopeful to see the successful completion of this project through award to APS, 
and thanks the DOE for the opportunity to provide funding to APS to bring this important project 
to life.  
 
Sincerely, 
 
Jason E. Whiting, Chairman 
Navajo County Board of Supervisors

Several public health events mark the month of April, and we wish to recognize them by dedicating
Navajo County to improving healthy outcomes for both humans and animals in our communities. To
achieve this goal, we request the board to declare April 14th-20th, 2024, as National Animal Care &
Control Appreciation Week 2024 in Navajo County. We also urge the board to encourage all citizens to
join us in expressing their sincere gratitude for the service and dedication of our Animal Care and
Control personnel.

Navajo County               
Proclamation 
 
Navajo County - For Official Use Only 
National Animal Care & Control Appreciation Week 
APRIL 14TH – 20TH, 2024 
WHEREAS, the National Animal Care and Control Association designated the second full week of 
April as National Animal and Control Appreciation Week; and 
WHEREAS, various federal, state, and local government officials throughout the country take this 
time to recognize, thank, and commend all Animal Control Officers and Animal Services Staff for the 
dedicated service they provide to the citizens, public safety, and domestic animals across the nation; 
and 
WHEREAS, everyday Animal Control Officers put themselves in potentially dangerous situations to 
ensure the safety and well-being of all animals and the public. Without their tireless efforts, many 
animals would suffer and could pose a threat to the community; and  
WHEREAS, Navajo County recognizes and commends the Animal Care & Control personnel who 
answer calls for assistance, capture roaming, and potentially dangerous animals, rescue animals, 
investigate report of animal abuse, educate pet owners about responsible care, and mediate 
disputes between neighbors regarding pets; and  
WHEREAS, The Board of Supervisors would like to officially recognize the hard work and dedication 
of all Animal Care & Control personnel of Navajo County and their assistance in caring for our four-
legged loved ones and their family members. 
 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT PROCLAIMED, by the Board of Supervisors of Navajo County that April 
14th-20th of 2024 is designated as “National Animal Care & Control Appreciation Week” in 
Navajo County and encourage all citizens to join us in expressing their sincere appreciation for the 
service and dedication of our Animal Care & Control personnel.  
 
PASSED, ADOPTED AND APPROVED by the Board of Supervisors on April 9th, 2024. 
 
 
            ____________________________ 
                                                                                                                                                 Jason Whiting, Chairman

_________________________________ 
Melissa W. Buckley, Clerk of the Board

Board of Supervisors Regular 4. b.        
Meeting Date: 04/09/2024  
Title: Proclamation for National Volunteer Week
Submitted For: David Clouse, Sheriff 
Submitted By: Kimberley Willis, Sheriff's Office Finance Manager
Department: Sheriff 
Presented By: Sheriff David Clouse
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of a proclamation declaring the week beginning April 21st through April 27th, 2024, as
"National Volunteer Week" in Navajo County, Arizona. 
Background:
National Volunteer Week was established by President Richard Nixon in 1974 and has continued with
every sitting U.S. president each year, urging Americans to give time to their communities. National
Volunteer Week is an opportunity to recognize and honor the countless individuals who selflessly invest
in the lives of others. National Volunteer Week is an opportunity for communities and organizations
throughout the country to recognize volunteers for their selfless contributions and inspire new volunteers
to get involved. The Navajo County Sheriff's Office often relies on the services and support of the
volunteers and is excited to celebrate and thank all volunteers in Navajo County for their contributions in
our communities.
Recommendation: 
We recommend the approval and adoption of a proclamation declaring the week beginning April 14th
through April 20th, 2024, as "National Volunteer Week" in Navajo County, Arizona, in honor of the men
and women who selflessly donate time and resources to keep our county and citizens safe.

Board of Supervisors Regular 6. a.        
Meeting Date: 04/09/2024  
Title: Supply of Aggregate for Cover Materials B24-02-027
Submitted For: Madhav Mundle, Public Works Director 
Submitted By: Cheryl Hollins, Account Specialist
Department: Public Works
Presented By: Madhav Mundle
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of award for Supply of Aggregate for Cover Material Contract Number B24-02-027 to
Perkins Cinders, Inc, Hatch Construction and Paving, Inc. and Brimhall Sand Rock and Building
Materials effective April 11, 2024 through April 10, 2025.
Background:
The purpose of these annual contracts is to supply Navajo County's road maintenance operation with the
aggregate rock material used for chip seal projects as part of its preventive maintenance program. 
Awarding contracts to multiple local vendors who provide material at multiple locations throughout the
County is operationally and financially beneficial to the County.  
Sealed proposals were received by the Board of Supervisors at the Navajo County Government Center,
Holbrook, Arizona until 3:00 p.m. M.S.T., March 28, 2024 in strict accordance with specifications on file
in the office of the Navajo County Department of Public Works.  No bids were accepted after 3:00 p.m.
M.S.T.  The bids were publicly opened and read aloud at 3:15 p.m. 
Navajo County may award contracts to all bidders for each item and select the bidder at the time of
purchase based on price, convenience, availability, and/or quality.  Three bids were received with an
average cost increase of 27.26% for materials (excluding hauling) compared to last year.  The award of
contracts to all bidders allows adequate coverage for materials by location. 
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends approval.
Fiscal Impact
Fiscal Year: 2024/2025
Budgeted Y/N: Y
Amount Requested:
Fiscal Impact:
The Public Works budget for FY 2024-2025 includes funding for road maintenance materials.

Board of Supervisors Regular 6. b. 1. a.        
Meeting Date: 04/09/2024  
Title: Task 3 Winslow Levee Survey to the Engineering Consultant Contract B23-02-015 with
HDR Engineering, Inc.
Submitted For: Madhav Mundle, Public Works Director 
Submitted By: Jeanine Carruthers, Deputy Director Administration
Department: Public Works
Presented By: Madhav Mundle
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of a Contract for Professional Services with HDR Engineering, Inc., for Engineering
Consultant Contract B23-02-015 for Task 3 Winslow Levee Survey. 
Background:
The purpose of this contract is to perform survey work for the Winslow Levee Design effort. Navajo
County Flood Control District will perform engineering survey and aerial mapping work for the levee
system. The said work will cover the segment of the Winslow Levee along the Little Colorado River and
the Ruby Wash Diversion Levee that was constructed by the US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) and
maintained by the City of Winslow. The final product will be used by the USACE design team for the
Winslow Levee design and construction. This work will be performed by utilizing Non-Federal funds as a
part of the Work in Kind (WIK) contribution from the Navajo County.
Recommendation: 
Staff recommend approval.
Fiscal Impact
Fiscal Year: FY2024
Budgeted Y/N: Y
Amount Requested: 288390.00
Fiscal Impact:
Funds are budgeted under Capital Outlay.

AGREEMENT made as of March 26, 2024, between Navajo County Flood Control 
District ("District") and HDR Engineering, Inc. (“Consultant”). 
 
WHEREAS, District requires cer tain professional serv ices for Engineering 
Consultant, Contract No. B23-02-015, Task 3 Winslow Levee Survey (“Project”); and 
 
WHEREAS, Consultant represents that it has the necessary expertise to provide such 
services in accordance with the terms of this Agreement. 
 
NOW, THEREFORE, the parties agree as follows: 
 
1. Services.  Consultant shall perform the work described in the Scope of Work dated 
February 19, 2024, and those additional items set forth in the Consultant’s schedule 
and fee proposal dated February 21, 2024, in a competent and professional manner to 
the satisfaction of District.  The Scope of Work and the Consultant’s schedule and fee 
proposal are attached hereto and by this reference incorporat ed herein.  If any 
incorporated term is inconsistent with the Agreement, this Agreement shall control. 
 
2. Consultant’s Expertise.  Consultant warrants that it has the ability, authority, 
capacity and professional expertise to perfo rm this Agreement.  Consultant shall 
provide an adequate staff of experienced  personnel, capable of and devoted to the 
successful accomplishment of the work to be performed hereunder.  Consultant shall 
assign specific individuals to key positio ns.  Once assigned to work under this 
Agreement, key personnel shall not be removed or replaced without District’s prior 
written approval.  
 
3. Independent Contractor.  Consultant acknowledges that  it is an independent 
contractor.  Neither party is or shall purport to be an agent, employee, partner, joint 
venturer or associate of the other.  An employee or agen t of one party shall not be 
deemed an employer or agent  of the other party for any purpose.  Taxes or Social 
Security contributions will not be with held from any paymen t by District, and 
Consultant shall be solely responsible for such matters.

shall impose on the subcontractor substantially the same obligations as are imposed 
on Consultant by this Agreement with respect to those matters covered by Sections 8, 
9, 10, 12, 15 and 18.  Consultant is  responsible for full performance of this 
Agreement regardless of whether subcontractors are used. 
 
5. Time for Completion.  Consultant’s services will be provided in a manner consistent 
with the degree of care and skill ordi narily exercised by me mbers of the same 
profession currently practicing under similar circumstances.  Consultant’s services 
shall be performed as expeditiously as is consistent with professional skill and care 
and the orderly progress of the Project, and in accord ance with an agreed upon 
schedule for the performance of the Services hereunder.  Time limits established by a 
schedule approved by District shall not, except for reasonable cause, be exceeded by 
District or Consultant.  The Schedule shall be adjusted, if necessary, as the Project 
proceeds.  The date for final performance shall be extended by the number of days 
that performance is delayed by governmental approval or review procedures or other 
causes beyond Consultant’s reasonable control, as jointly confirmed in writing by the 
parties’ representatives. 
 
6. Payment.  District shall pay to Consultant  a not-to-exceed su m of two hundred 
eighty-eight thousand three hundred ninety dollars ($288,390.00) as payment in full 
for all services rendered by Consultant pursuant to this Agreement.  Payments shall 
be made within 30 days of District’s receipt of Consultant’s monthly invoices.  Each 
invoice shall detail the work performed during the billing period.

resolved.

Thank you for the opportunity to submit this cost proposal for the above-referenced project.

Scope of Work 
Painted Sky Engineering & Survey, LLC shall provide the Services and Deliverable(s) as follows:  
Task 1 – Research Existing Mapping and Control 
Painted Sky Engineering & Survey, LLC (PSES) shall work in conjunction with AeroTech Mapping to provide 
a mapping survey for the Winslow Levee  project. The mapping for the 5 -ft contour interval will cover 
approximately 14,800 acres and the mapping for the 1 -ft contour interval will cover approximately 2,500 
acres (most of the 2,500-acre area is located within the 14,800-acre area). The approximate boundary of 
these areas is shown in Figure 1. PSES will research existing mapping and control for the area. This first task 
allows for the preparation of the fieldwork. 
 
Task 2 – Establish Primary Control 
PSES shall establish primary control throughout the site. The primary control will include an existing NGS 
monument at the south end of the project and 2 new monuments to be set by PS ES. One of these new 
monuments will be near the middle of the project and the other will be near the North end of the project. 
The new monuments will be brass caps attached to rebar set in concrete. 
 
Task 3 – Establish Local Project Control 
PSES shall establish local project control that will be tied into the primary control points. This includes the 
setting of approximately 16 new monuments. These will a lso be brass caps  attached to rebar set in 
concrete. The local project control will also include county monuments that have been used in the past. 
PSES may include some of those monuments, but we will establish new horizontal and vertical coordinates 
for them.  
 
Task 4 – U-SMART Control Sheets 
PSES shall provide a spreadsheet containing information regarding the primary and local project control.  
The spreadsheet will include the Station Name, Latitude, Longitude, North Coordinate, East Coordinate, 
Units of Measure  (International Feet), Horizontal Datum  (NAD83, Zone (GeoID 18 - Arizona East 201) , H-
EPOCH (2010), Elevation, and Vertical Datum  (NAVD88).  PSES shall also provide a scale factor to tie 
between grid and ground coordinates for the project.   PSES shall also provide two photos (Horizon and 
Close-Up) of each control monument as required for the completion of the U-SMART form. 
 
Task 5 – 1 Foot Aerial Mapping (2,500 Acres) 
PSES shall set and survey approximately 36 aerial control panels throughout the 1-ft contour interval area. 
PSES will also provide supplemental survey ing for various infrastructure throughout the site including 
fences/walls, drain inlet and outlet structures, 4 bridge crossings, and the ground in vegetated areas. PSES 
shall provide geometry and mapping for the bridge crossing s. PSES shall also provide supplemental 
labeling of the area, not including the labeling of residential and commercial areas.   PSES sh all also 
include control information for the mapping panels in the same format as the primary and local control.

<!-- page 674 -->
P:\M Drive Marketing\Arizona PY-SL\2024 PROPOSALS\028\Winslow Levee Aerial Mapping Survey PSA Revised.docx  Page 3 of 8 
 
 
 
Task 6 – 5 Foot Aerial Mapping (14,800 Acres) 
PSES shall set and survey approximately 11 aerial control panels throughout the 5-ft contour interval area. 
PSES will also provide a quality control plan  per the SOW requirements and the sample provided , 
spreadsheets for primary and local control, a control map on mylar, supplemental labeling (excluding 
residential and commercial areas), and quality control check points.   PSES shall also include control 
information for the mapping panels in the same format as the primary and local control.  
 
Task 7 – Quality Control Evaluation 
PSES shall send a different survey crew with a different set of GPS equipment out to the site for a quality 
control evaluation. This will ensure that the coordinates for the control network are correct and that 
outside parties will be able to tie into the network. 
 
Task 8 – Meetings 
This task accounts for any meetings that PSES may need to attend for the project.  
 
Task 9 – Project Management 
This task accounts for all communication with Navajo County, AeroTech, and HDR as well as 
interdepartmental communication throughout the duration of the project.  
 
PSES proposes to provide these services on a Lump Sum basis for a fee of $143,750.00. These services will 
be invoiced monthly, based on the amount of work that is completed each month.  
 
Exclusions: 
Items that are specifically excluded from this proposal and if required, can be provided at an additional 
fee are the following: 
• Record of Surveys for Right of Ways 
• Construction Staking
